groups.title: Audio guide — information
groups.instruction: Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.

parts.context: A museum guide describes the galleries on the ground floor and the audio guide service.

transcript.text: Hello, everyone, and welcome to the City History Museum. I'm Ms Hart, and before you pick up your audio guides, I'd like to show you how the ground floor is arranged. Please look at the plan on the back of your ticket.
transcript.speaker: MS HART

transcript.text: You've just entered from the left of the plan and you are now standing in the main hall. This is where you can buy tickets, leave your coats and find the toilets, and it's also where we hold our special events.
transcript.speaker: MS HART

transcript.text: If you need any help, our staff wear red badges, so please ask them if you can't find something. They know the collection very well and love talking to visitors.
transcript.speaker: MS HART

transcript.text: Let's go through the galleries one by one. If you turn to the top left of the plan, the first room is Ancient Coins. It contains more than three hundred coins found in the city, some of them over two thousand years old.
transcript.speaker: MS HART

transcript.text: Next to it, in the middle at the top, is the Pottery Gallery. The oldest pot here is nearly five thousand years old, and my favourite piece is a small blue bowl that was probably used for oil.
transcript.speaker: MS HART

transcript.text: In the top right corner is the Textiles Room. It's quite dark, because the old fabrics are sensitive to light, so please don't use flash photography in there.
transcript.speaker: MS HART

transcript.text: Directly across the main hall, on the right-hand side of the plan, is the Egyptian Gallery. It's our most popular room, particularly with school groups, because it has a real mummy.
transcript.speaker: MS HART

transcript.text: At the bottom right is the café, and in the middle at the bottom is the gift shop. You can visit both without a ticket, so many local people come just for lunch.
transcript.speaker: MS HART

transcript.text: And in the bottom left corner is the Children's Discovery Room, where young visitors can try on costumes and handle replica objects. It's much noisier than the other rooms, so I'd suggest visiting it last.
transcript.speaker: MS HART

transcript.text: Now, a few details about the audio guide. It's available in six languages: English, French, German, Spanish, Chinese and Arabic. Please choose when you collect the headset at the desk.
transcript.speaker: MS HART

transcript.text: All the languages are spoken by native speakers, and we recorded them in a studio, so the sound is very clear.
transcript.speaker: MS HART

transcript.text: The guide costs three pounds, plus a deposit of ten pounds, which we return when you give back the headset. You can pay by card or cash, but we cannot accept foreign banknotes.
transcript.speaker: MS HART

transcript.text: The tour takes about ninety minutes if you listen to everything. However, you don't have to follow the order. Each room has numbered signs, so you can type the number into the handset and hear that section.
transcript.speaker: MS HART

transcript.text: There's also a version for children, with games and questions, which is free for anyone under twelve. And for visitors with poor eyesight, we offer a description of the main objects and the layout of each gallery.
transcript.speaker: MS HART

transcript.text: The museum closes at five thirty, and the audio guides must be returned by five o'clock, so please keep an eye on the time. Enjoy your visit.
transcript.speaker: MS HART
